title: MMR vaccine (measles, mumps, rubella)
what: A single vaccine shot against three diseases: measles, rubella, and mumps. Children usually get it twice.
why: For children on the schedule, usually at 1 year and 6 years. For adults without two doses, on a doctor's advice.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds, with the checkup usually 15 to 40 minutes
tell_doctor: If your child is ill now or has a fever
Immune system conditions, or treatment that weakens immunity
If blood products were given recently
If you are pregnant or planning a pregnancy

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when your child is well. They will be checked first.

prepare.title: Your child
prepare.text: Bring a favorite toy to distract your little one.

prepare.title: Pregnancy
prepare.text: For adult women: it is best to avoid getting pregnant for a month after the vaccine.

steps: The doctor asks how your child is and takes their temperature
You hold your child on your lap
The skin is wiped, and the shot is given in the upper arm or thigh
After the shot, sit in the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: A quick prick. Your child may cry a little
Sometimes, 5 to 12 days later, a mild fever or rash. It is a reaction to the vaccine
Sometimes the cheeks or neck swell a little
after: Stay near the room for 30 minutes
A rash after the vaccine is not contagious
The second dose follows the schedule
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a rash all over: call emergency services
A seizure with a fever: call emergency services

faq.q: Why did a fever start a week later?
faq.a: It is a live weakened vaccine, so the response can come later. It usually passes in 1 to 2 days.

faq.q: Is it true this vaccine causes autism?
faq.a: No. Large studies have not found that.
If you have not had two doses, or do not know, ask your doctor.

reminders.text: MMR vaccine tomorrow. Your child should be well. Bring the vaccination record.
